To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nutrient availability affects the C:P ratio of DOM and that this ratio affects CO2 losses from the litter layer in nutrient-poor tropical rain forests.

1) litter layer organic matter decomposition is rapid in tropical rain forests; 2) litter layer decomposition is dominated by the rapid leaching of DOM, not by direct mineralization; and 3) P fertilization stimulates microbial mineralization of the leached DOM in soil, leading to increased CO2 losses.
nutrient addition stimulates P uptake by decomposing material, resulting in higher P content of soluble DOM, which in turn stimulates microbial mineralization and CO2 loss from the soil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the availability of nutrients such as nitrogen (N) or phosphorus (P), which are essential for plant growth and development, affects decomposition of leaf litter in tropical forests.
the regulation of decomposition in tropical forests, which are the dominant terrestrial ecosystem in terms of carbon (C) storage and C fluxes to the atmosphere.
the role of nutrient availability in regulating organic matter decomposition in the litter layer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nutrient availability affects organic matter decomposition in tropical rain forests by regulating microbial mineralization of dissolved organic matter leached from the leaf litter layer.
P fertilization increased microbial mineralization of leached organic matter, and that this effect was mediated by the P content of leachate.

nutrient availability does not affect mass loss in decomposing material in nutrient-poor ecosystems, but that it may regulate CO2 emissions by stimulating the mineralization of DOM that leaches from the litter layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in tropical ecosystems with a high rainfall and low P content, the litter layer acts as a filter for DOM that is leached from decomposing material.

in nutrient-poor tropical forests, nutrient limitation of decomposition is likely to be a result of P limitation of DOM mineralization in the soil rather than of N or P limitation of litter-layer mass loss.

nutrient availability affects the fate of organic matter in the litter layer and that the effects of nutrients on organic matter decomposition in tropical rain forests may not be as simple as we once thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nutrient limitation of decomposition in nutrient-peninsula tropical forests is not likely to be as important as in temperate and boreal ecosystems.
nutrient limitation of microbial mineralization can have important effects on C storage in nutrient-poor ecosystems.
, even in nutrient-poor ecosystems where mass loss is rapid, nutrient limitation of microbial processes can still regulate C storage.
